title: Has the time not come for your heart to soften?
subtitle: A gentle question before the heart hardens
then: Ibn Mas'ud said only four years passed between his group accepting Islam and this verse, {idea}in which Allah subtly admonished us.{/idea} It asks believers if it is time for their hearts to be humbled by the Quran. It warns against becoming like earlier people who, as time stretched on, {trap}grew hard and stopped accepting advice.{/trap}
now: You have heard the Friday talk on death so many times you check your phone during it. The verse you cried at years ago now plays in the car like background music. {trap}That is how hardness arrives: slowly, through familiarity.{/trap} The question is addressed to believers. To you.
old: I already know all this. I have heard it before.
new: Hearing it often is exactly when my heart needs to stay soft.
try: Listen to one short surah today with no other screen open, and let it reach you.

title: Dead ground comes back to life. So can a hard heart.
subtitle: Rain for the earth, Quran for the heart

row.title: my heart is too hard now

then: Right after the warning about hard hearts comes hope. Ibn Kathir says this verse shows Allah {reward}brings softness to hearts after they have become hard{/reward}, guides the confused, and relieves hardship. Just as He revives dry land with rain, {idea}He guides hardened hearts with the proofs of the Quran.{/idea}
now: That patch of brown grass by the bus stop. Three days of rain and it is green again, as if nothing happened. You feel numb in prayer lately, like nothing moves you. {reward}That ground is not finished. Neither are you.{/reward}
old: Once my heart goes cold, it stays cold.
new: The One who greens dead land can soften my heart again.
try: Make one dua today: O Allah, revive my heart the way You revive the earth.

title: Men and women who give, lending to Allah.
subtitle: Charity with a good heart, multiplied
then: The verse names both men and women who give. Ibn Kathir explains a goodly loan as giving {idea}with a good heart, seeking the pleasure of Allah{/idea}, not worldly rewards or thanks from those who receive. He says Allah multiplies it {reward}from tenfold up to seven hundredfold and more.{/reward}
now: You paid for the old man's groceries at the till and he did not even notice. Part of you wanted him to. {idea}The verse says that is the best version of it.{/idea} No thank-you note needed. The Receiver already counted it.
old: If no one notices what I give, it hardly matters.
new: Giving unseen, wanting only Allah's pleasure, is the loan He multiplies.
try: Give something today in a way the person cannot thank you for.

title: True believers stand among the highest ranks.
subtitle: The Siddiqun, the martyrs, and their light
then: Ibn Mas'ud described three categories here: those who give, the Siddiqun, and the martyrs. Ibn Kathir cites the hadith where people asked if Paradise's lofty mansions were only for prophets. The Prophet ﷺ said no: {reward}they are for men who believe in Allah and believe the Messengers.{/reward} Each will have {idea}reward and light, by their deeds.{/idea}
now: You assume the top ranks belong to famous scholars and saints, not someone who works a night shift and prays tired. But the Prophet ﷺ described those mansions as for {reward}people who believed and trusted.{/reward} That door is open to you.
old: The highest ranks are for special people, not ordinary believers like me.
new: Sincere, truthful faith can reach ranks I thought were out of reach.
try: Do one thing today with complete honesty, even when a small lie would be easier.

title: This life is a green field that turns to straw.
subtitle: Play, show, boasting, and counting
then: Ibn Kathir explains the parable: rain falls after despair, the crop grows and pleases the farmers, then {trap}turns yellow and becomes straw.{/trap} This is the world, he says, and also each person: young and strong, then old and frail. He cites the hadith that {idea}Paradise is nearer to you than your sandal strap, and so is the Fire.{/idea}
now: The car you saved for. The followers count. Comparing kids' grades in the parents' chat. {trap}Play, show, boasting, counting.{/trap} Look at photos of yourself from ten years ago. The green field is already turning.
old: Getting more and showing it off is what makes life worth it.
new: This world is a season that fades. What lasts is forgiveness and His pleasure.
try: Notice one thing today you were about to show off. Keep it private instead.

title: Race, but toward forgiveness, not more stuff.
subtitle: A Garden as wide as the heavens and earth

row.title: a Garden
sub: as wide as heaven and earth

key.label: What the poor can race with

then: After the race for wealth in the last verse, this one names the right race. Ibn Kathir cites the hadith of the poor emigrants who worried the wealthy would surpass them by giving charity. The Prophet ﷺ taught them to {reward}glorify, praise and magnify Allah thirty-three times after every prayer.{/reward} {idea}It is all His bounty, given to whom He wills.{/idea}
now: Everyone in your office is racing: the bigger house, the better school, the next title. You can stay in your lane and still be racing. {reward}After your next prayer, thirty-three, thirty-three, thirty-three.{/reward} Nobody else needs to know who is ahead.
old: I cannot compete in good deeds with people who have more money.
new: The race to forgiveness is open to everyone, even with empty pockets.
try: After one prayer today, say subhan Allah, alhamdulillah, and Allahu akbar 33 times each.

title: Nothing hits you that was not already written.
subtitle: Every hardship known before it happened
then: Ibn Kathir explains that Allah measured and recorded all things before He created them. Qatadah said the calamity on earth is famine, and in yourselves, suffering and disease. He cites the hadith that {idea}Allah ordained the measures of everything fifty thousand years before creating the heavens and earth.{/idea}
now: The phone call from the doctor. The redundancy email at 9:02 on a Monday. It feels like the floor vanished. {idea}But it did not catch Allah by surprise.{/idea} It was known, measured, and nothing about it is beyond Him.
old: When disaster hits, it means everything is out of control.
new: Nothing reaches me that Allah did not already know and measure.
try: When something goes wrong today, say: this was written, and Allah is with me in it.

title: So you do not despair over losses or brag over gains.
subtitle: Why knowing about destiny brings calm
then: Ibn Kathir explains: Allah told you of His decree so that you know {idea}what met you would never have missed you, and what missed you would never have met you.{/idea} Do not boast, since it is not your effort alone. Ikrimah said: everyone feels joy and grief, {reward}so make your joy gratitude and your grief patience.{/reward}
now: Your cousin got the job you applied for. You see the post and feel sick. A year later you get a promotion and want to post about it right away. {idea}Same verse covers both moments.{/idea} Neither the loss nor the win is the whole story.
old: What I missed was stolen from me, and what I got, I earned.
new: What missed me was never mine. What came to me was a gift.
try: Think of one recent loss and one gain. Say sabr for the first, shukr for the second.

title: Stingy, and teaching others to be stingy too.
subtitle: Allah does not need what you hold back

row.title: He is Free of need
sub: only I lose by turning away

then: This follows the warning about boasting. Ibn Kathir explains these are people who {trap}commit evil and encourage others to commit it.{/trap} Whoever turns away, Allah is Rich and Praiseworthy, as Musa said: {idea}if you and all on earth disbelieve, Allah is still Free of need.{/idea}
now: Someone mentions donating at a family dinner and you say, charities just waste it anyway. Everyone nods and the moment passes. {trap}One sentence, and you taught the whole table to hold back.{/trap}
old: Talking people out of giving is just being sensible with money.
new: Holding back, and teaching others to hold back, only costs me. Allah needs nothing.
try: Next time someone talks about giving, encourage them instead of doubting.

title: A Book, a Balance, and iron, so people live by justice.
subtitle: The verse that names the surah
then: Ibn Kathir says the Balance is justice, according to Mujahid and Qatadah. Iron has {idea}mighty power and many benefits{/idea}: coins, hammers, axes, saws, tools for farming and cooking. All of it shows who supports Allah and His messengers unseen. {idea}Allah does not need anyone's help{/idea}; it is a test of intentions.
now: The hammer in your toolbox, the steel in your car, the knife you chop onions with. Strength and usefulness in your hands every day. {idea}The question is what you build with it, and why.{/idea} Fairness at work, at home, when no one is checking.
old: Power and tools are neutral. It does not matter how I use them.
new: Everything strong in my hands comes with a Balance, a call to be just.
try: Today, in one decision that affects someone else, ask: is this fair to them?

title: Prophethood ran in families, but guidance did not.
subtitle: The line of Nuh and Ibrahim

row.title: good family, so I am fine

then: Ibn Kathir explains that every prophet after Nuh came from his offspring, and every book and messenger after Ibrahim came from Ibrahim's line. {reward}Prophethood and scripture were placed in their families.{/reward} Yet the verse says plainly: {trap}some were guided, but many were disobedient.{/trap}
now: Your grandfather was the imam. Your mother never missed a prayer. You grew up hearing Quran in the house. {idea}That is a gift, not a guarantee.{/idea} The verse speaks to the person who leans on family and forgets to choose.
old: I come from a religious family, so I am on the right path.
new: A blessed family line opens the door. I still have to walk through it.
try: Thank Allah for one person who passed faith to you, then do one act of faith yourself.

title: Mercy in their hearts, and a burden they invented.
subtitle: Compassion given, extra rules not kept

picture.label: What the followers of Isa had

then: Ibn Kathir explains that Allah placed {reward}compassion and mercy{/reward} in the hearts of those who followed Isa. Monasticism they invented themselves. He says the verse criticises two things: {trap}adding to the religion what Allah did not legislate, then not fulfilling what they took on.{/trap} Those who believed were still rewarded.
now: The new year when you vow to pray every night prayer, fast every Monday and Thursday, and read a juz a day. By February you have dropped all of it, and feel worse than before. {idea}Do what was asked, gently and steadily.{/idea} Keep what you commit to.
old: The more extra I pile on myself, the closer I get to Allah.
new: Mercy and steady obedience matter more than burdens I invent and drop.
try: Pick one small good habit you can actually keep, and do it today.

title: A double share of mercy, and light to walk by.
subtitle: What taqwa and faith in the Messenger ﷺ bring
then: Ibn Kathir cites the parable the Prophet ﷺ gave: a man hired workers, some from dawn to midday, some to Asr. The last group worked from Asr to sunset and {reward}received double.{/reward} When the earlier groups complained, he asked if he had wronged them. They said no. {idea}It is My grace, which I give to whom I will.{/idea}
now: You came to practice late. Your friend has prayed since age seven, and you only started at thirty. You feel behind. The parable says the late shift was paid twice. {reward}Keep going until sunset.{/reward}
old: I started late, so I will always be behind in reward.
new: Allah's mercy is not measured in hours. Those who keep going are given double.
try: Ask Allah today for a double portion of His mercy and a light to walk by.

title: All bounty is in Allah's hand alone.
subtitle: No one controls who receives His grace
then: The surah ends with the conclusion of the parable of the workers. Ibn Kathir says it is so they know {idea}they cannot prevent what Allah gives, or give what Allah prevents.{/idea} The verse closes on one note: {reward}Allah is the possessor of great bounty.{/reward}
now: The manager who seems to hold your future. The relative who thinks they decide who inherits. The committee that reviews your application. {idea}None of them hold the real key.{/idea} Do your best with them, and trust the Hand that actually gives.
old: My future depends on who likes me and who is in charge.
new: No one can block what Allah gives me or give what He holds back.
try: Before one stressful meeting or message today, say: all bounty is in Your hand.
